name: Shammah
overview: Shammah was a male Edomite figure known primarily as the son of Reuel and a chief among the Edomites. His role as a leader within the Edomite tribe highlights his prominence in the genealogical records of Genesis. There are no additional notes on his life or character beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammah means "waste" in Hebrew. This is the only recorded name for him, and it is not indicated that the name was given by God. The meaning itself does not have further explanation in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Shammah is explicitly identified as the son of Reuel, establishing his immediate family connection. Scripture does not provide further family relationships beyond this father-son link.
scriptureSignificance: Shammah's significance lies in his position as a chief of Edom, which marks him as a person of authority and leadership within the Edomite people. Being listed among the descendants of Reuel situates him within the broader narrative of Edomite genealogy, which is important for understanding the lineage and tribal leadership structures in the Old Testament. His mention underscores the continuity of leadership among the Edomites as recorded in Genesis.
